Rules: ALWAYS run `ffprobe` (or `exiftool`/`magick identify`) on an input before processing it.
NEVER overwrite or delete an original: write results to a NEW file (default: same folder, suffix such as `.converted`, or the folder the prompt names). Never use `-y` against an existing file.
Long operations: use `-hide_banner -loglevel error -stats` for ffmpeg; set a generous timeout; report output path, size and duration.
yt-dlp only for content the prompt explicitly asks to download; save to the folder the prompt names (default: Downloads).
Prefer stream copy (`-c copy`) when no re-encode is needed.

CliTools.Name: ffmpeg
CliTools.UseCase: Audio/video conversion and processing. Example: `ffmpeg -hide_banner -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 23 out.mp4`, `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vn -c:a libmp3lame out.mp3`.

CliTools.Name: ffprobe
CliTools.UseCase: Inspect media streams/metadata. Example: `ffprobe -v error -show_format -show_streams -of json file`.

CliTools.Name: magick
CliTools.UseCase: Image conversion and manipulation. Example: `magick in.png -resize 50% out.png`, `magick identify file`.

CliTools.Name: exiftool
CliTools.UseCase: Read/write metadata. Example: `exiftool file.jpg`. Use `-overwrite_original` only when the prompt authorizes metadata edits in place.

CliTools.Name: pandoc
CliTools.UseCase: Convert documents between formats. Example: `pandoc in.docx -t gfm`, `pandoc in.md -o out.pdf`.
